chunks: And it is narrated from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not close for a believer a door of sustenance except that Allah opens for him that which is better than it.

key_terms.بَابَ: a door or avenue, meaning a means or opening
key_terms.رِزْقٍ: sustenance or provision granted by Allah
key_terms.مُؤْمِنٍ: a believer, the one addressed as recipient of divine care

ai.seo_question: What does Islam teach when a believer loses a source of livelihood?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that when a believer loses one avenue of provision, Allah عزّ وجلّ grants something better in its place. It encourages trust in Allah’s wisdom and hope during financial or worldly hardship.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3611 - It is narrated from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdullah (as):
"Allah (swt), the Almighty and Glorious, does not close a door of sustenance for a believer except that He opens for him what is better than it."
